In 6-dimensional [[geometry]], there are 35 [[uniform 6-polytope|uniform polytopes]] with A<sub>6</sub> symmetry. There is one self-dual regular form, the [[6-simplex]] with 7 vertices.

Each can be visualized as symmetric [[orthographic projection]]s in [[Coxeter plane]]s of the A<sub>6</sub> Coxeter group, and other subgroups.

== Graphs ==
Symmetric [[orthographic projection]]s of these 35 polytopes can be made in the A<sub>6</sub>, A<sub>5</sub>, A<sub>4</sub>, A<sub>3</sub>, A<sub>2</sub> [[Coxeter plane]]s. A<sub>k</sub> graphs have ''[k+1]'' symmetry. For even k and symmetric ringed diagrams, symmetry doubles to ''[2(k+1)]''.

These 35 polytopes are each shown in these 5 symmetry planes, with vertices and edges drawn, and vertices colored by the number of overlapping vertices in each projective position.
